name: TLP2361(TPL,E
title: TLP2361: 15 MBd high-speed logic-output photocoupler, totem-pole inverting output, 2.7 V to 5.5 V, -40 °C to 125 °C, SO6
summary: A single-channel digital photocoupler: a GaAlAs infrared LED drives a high-gain detector IC with a push-pull inverting logic output, so the output is low while the LED is lit. It runs from 2.7 V to 5.5 V at no more than 1 mA supply current, switches at 15 MBd typical, and needs at most 1.6 mA of LED current to switch at 125 °C. An internal Faraday shield gives at least ±20 kV/µs common-mode transient immunity, and the SO6 package isolates 3750 Vrms with 5 mm creepage and clearance.
key_figures: 1.3 mA max to 105 °C, 1.6 mA max to 125 °C
tpHL 49 ns typ, tpLH 39 ns typ, 80 ns max

notes: In an order code TPL is the tape type and E marks RoHS compatibility; V4 adds EN60747-5-5 approval. For safety-standard applications the standard type number TLP2361 is used.

circuits.title: VOL test circuit
circuits.description: A current source pushes IF into the anode and takes it back from the cathode, so the LED is lit and the output is low. The supply sits across VCC and GND with 0.1 µF beside it. A second current source forces IO into the output pin while a voltmeter from VO to ground reads the low-level output voltage.

parts.note: current source; current leaves at OUT
current source; current leaves at OUT, into pin 5

circuits.title: VOH test circuit
circuits.description: The LED pins are left open, so the output is high. The VCC rail is the grounded reference. A current source draws IO out of the output pin into the VCC rail, and a voltmeter between VCC and VO reads the drop VO; the high-level output voltage is VCC minus that reading. 0.1 µF bypasses VCC to GND.

parts.note: current source; current enters at IN from pin 5

circuits.title: ICCL test circuit
circuits.description: With IF driven through the LED from a current source, the output is low and its pin is left open. An ammeter between the supply and pin 6 reads the low-level supply current; 0.1 µF bypasses pin 6 to pin 4 on the device side of the meter.

parts.note: current source; current leaves at OUT

circuits.title: ICCH test circuit
circuits.description: The same supply-current measurement with the LED pins open, so the output is high; the output pin is also open.

circuits.title: Switching time test circuit
circuits.description: A pulse generator delivering 2 mA pulses at 5 MHz, 50 % duty, edges faster than 5 ns, drives the LED through R1 into the anode, with R2 from the cathode to ground; RT = R1 + R2 = 1.68 kΩ. The output carries only CL, about 15 pF of probe and wiring capacitance, and is watched at VO. Delays are taken between the 50 % points of the input current and of the output; fall and rise times between 90 % and 10 % of the output swing.

circuits.title: Common-mode transient immunity test circuit
circuits.description: The LED is fed through R1 into the anode and R2 out of the cathode, RT = R1 + R2 = 1.68 kΩ. Switch position A connects a battery that sets IF = 2 mA (output low, for CML); position B shorts the input so IF = 0 mA (output high, for CMH). A 1000 V pulse source VCM sits between the input-side common node and the output ground. CMH is the steepest edge for which VO stays above 2.3 V (VCC = 3.3 V) or 4 V (VCC = 5.0 V); CML is the steepest for which VO stays below 1 V.

operation.text: A high-output GaAlAs infrared LED shines across the isolation gap onto a high-gain, high-speed photodetector IC. The detector drives a totem-pole output of two MOSFETs (M1 to VCC, M2 to GND), and the logic is inverting: LED on gives a low output, LED off a high one. A Faraday shield inside the package between LED and detector guarantees ±20 kV/µs of common-mode transient immunity. Data rate is 15 MBd typical (NRZ).
Operation is guaranteed from 2.7 V to 5.5 V and from -40 °C up to 125 °C. Supply current is at most 1.0 mA in either output state (ICCL, ICCH).

The LED is on at 2 mA to 6 mA and off with its voltage held between 0 V and 0.8 V. Edges of the input current take less than 0.5 µs. The threshold input current IFHL is at most 1.3 mA up to 105 °C and 1.6 mA up to 125 °C, which lets a microcontroller drive the LED directly at low current. For the switching figures the LED resistance is split, R1 = R2 = 840 Ω on anode and cathode, totalling RT = 1.68 kΩ.

A 0.1 µF ceramic capacitor between VCC (pin 6) and GND (pin 4) is needed to stabilise the high-gain linear amplifier; without it the coupler may not switch properly. It is placed no more than 1 cm from either pin.

tpHL runs from the input current crossing 50 % on its rise to the output falling through 50 %; tpLH from the input falling through 50 % to the output rising through 50 %. Fall and rise times are taken between the 90 % and 10 % output levels. Pulse width distortion is |tpHL - tpLH|; skew tpsk is the widest spread of tpHL or tpLH between units under the same supply, input current and temperature.

A 1000 V pulse is applied between the input and output grounds. CMH, with IF = 0 mA, is the steepest edge that keeps the output above 2.3 V at VCC = 3.3 V or 4 V at VCC = 5.0 V; CML, with IF = 2 mA, the steepest that keeps it below 1 V. The slew rate is the 800 V between the 10 % and 90 % points divided by the edge time.
Isolation ratings are measured with the part treated as two terminals: pins 1 and 3 shorted on one side and pins 4, 5 and 6 shorted on the other. The rating is 3750 Vrms for 60 s at R.H. ≤ 60 %.

UL1577 approved (file E67349), cUL under CSA Component Acceptance Service No. 5A (file E67349), CQC under GB4943.1 and GB8898 (Thailand factory), and VDE to EN60747-5-5 when ordered with option (V4). For safety-standard applications the standard type number TLP2361 is quoted.

Parts qualified to EN60747-5-5 carry V4 in the order code, e.g. TLP2361(V4-TPL,E(O, where TPL marks the tape packing and E RoHS compatibility. They have VIORM = 707 Vpeak, a 6000 Vpeak transient overvoltage rating and a V marked on the package beside the pin 1 dot.
The top face carries the Toshiba mark, a lot number, the code P2361 and a dot by pin 1.

Reflow is done once or twice, judged by package surface temperature, with no more than 2 weeks between the first and last mounting. Flow soldering is done once: preheat 60 s to 120 s at 150 °C, then 260 °C for up to 10 s. A soldering iron touches each lead once, for up to 10 s at 260 °C or 3 s at 350 °C.

Keep parts at 5 °C to 35 °C and 45 % to 75 % relative humidity, away from moisture, sunlight, corrosive gas, dust and mechanical load, and where temperature changes slowly so that no condensation forms on the leads. Use anti-static containers once parts leave their packing. After two years in storage, check the leads for solderability.
Factory networking, high-speed digital interfaces in instrumentation and control equipment, and I/O interface boards.
